title: Images and containers
summary: An image is a packaged starting point. A container is a running or stopped instance created from an image.
introduction: An image is a packaged starting point. A container is a running or stopped instance created from an image. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An image is a packaged starting point. A container is a running or stopped instance created from an image.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Docker commands need a local Docker installation. Pulling images needs internet access and storage. These examples are for a disposable practice environment, not this website's runtime.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Docker. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.
The command reports Docker client and engine versions when the engine is available. It does not run a container.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain an image as a recipe and a container as one use of that recipe.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Installing a command-line client alone does not mean the Docker engine is running.
For more detail later, use this [Docker further reading](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/).

seo.title: Docker: Images and containers
seo.description: Learn about images and containers in Docker. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
